races.name: C.J. Sheeran Ltd 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and style unknown, trained by John Joseph Hanlon who has one win from 15 in the last 14 days; the absence of any form string makes this an open book but the unknown factor is worth respecting in a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: Returned a ninth on debut over this exact 17f trip on Good ground at a track that suits, and while Archdeacon's 14-day record is modest, the horse's true nature as a hold-up type means it will be racing in traffic rather than from the rear it would prefer.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Durkan's yard has a quiet recent record and the horse's best flat form came on Standard, not Good; it carries the hold-up tag but in a field this large it will find itself buried in midfield rather than settled at the back as preferred, tempering confidence.

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: Shaped best of all on hurdles debut when runner-up over this 17f trip on Good ground, and the handicap mark reflects that potential; the hold-up style is genuine but getting the back-of-the-field position it thrives from is going to be extremely difficult against this many rivals, so the chance should be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Motherland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with no public form, carrying the unknown style tag, and Elliott has two wins from 46 in the past fortnight — debut hurdlers from this yard can be forward enough to feature but nothing in the data confirms that here.

runners_data.name: Mount Eden
runners_data.note: Landed third on hurdles debut over 16f on Good and Slevin takes the ride, but the tendency to fade in the finish is flagged and the horse's natural hold-up inclination will be squeezed out of position in this field — watch whether it can at least get a clear run late.

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: Sean Flanagan's mount showed a third on debut over 16f hurdles and has placed twice on Good ground from six tries at the going; as the one confirmed prominent type likely to track Words Unspoken, its tactical position is the most clearly defined in the race.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Harrington has three winners from 33 in the past 14 days which is the best recent trainer strike-rate in this field; the hold-up profile and a second in a 12f Flat maiden on Good are the key angles, but the horse remains lightly tried over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; form shows a seventh and fourth over this exact trip on Good ground and Enright rides, so the horse knows its job and is well-placed to control the fractions with no confirmed rival for the lead.

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: De Bromhead saddles with four winners from 35 over 14 days and O'Keeffe is a reliable pilot, but the horse has struggled to make an impact in flat form and its natural hold-up inclination means it will be hemmed into midfield rather than hunting from the back where it ideally operates.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Cromwell runner who was fourth on hurdles debut over 17f on Good, showing consistent placing at the distance and trip; the tongue-tie is noted, but as a genuine hold-up type in a packed field it faces the same positional headache as its stablemates in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Ran a creditable second over 10f on Good for Sexton but the pattern of fading finishes is flagged and the form is inconsistent; the hold-up style and apprentice booking (Lamon, 7lb claimer) add risk, and the horse is likely to race closer to mid-pack than the back it would prefer.

runners_data.name: Sofi's Gift
runners_data.note: Shaped promisingly when second over 16f on Good — the most directly relevant hurdles form in the field for a hold-up type; Finegan is a 5lb claimer, but the horse's staying profile and Good-ground form give it a genuine squeak if it can find clear air late.

races.paceDynamic: Words Unspoken is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner maiden hurdle and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Phillip Enright can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m½f trip on Good ground at Ballinrobe. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Mount Eden, Minella Buoy, Divine Believer, Connor Of Mali, Divelment, No Bother Aoife, Sofi's Gift, and Sands Castle are all natural rear-runners who are unlikely to secure their preferred position in a 13-runner field, pushing several into a midfield cluster they would not ordinarily occupy. Nicky Larson is the one genuine prominent runner likely to track Words Unspoken into the early stages, with the two unknown quantities Motherland and Camp Verde adding a degree of uncertainty given their lightly-raced profiles. The race shape strongly favours hold-up-to-prominent horses with stamina and a good cruising speed, as Words Unspoken's uncontested lead at a measured clip will compress the field until the final bend, rewarding those who can travel into contention late without burning energy fighting for position — a clean prominent-to-midfield profile with proven staying ability over this trip looks best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Words Unspoken Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Words Unspoken bowls clear uncontested and the field cannot close the gap from the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Enright sets a measured pace on the front end with Nicky Larson the only company, and the steady fractions mean Words Unspoken conserves enough to kick again off the last and hold on; the horse's hurdles form shows it stays this trip and acts on Good.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly crawling and a prominent-midfield mover picks off a tiring Words Unspoken from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Nicky Larson or one of the lightly-raced unknowns tracks smoothly into contention without over-exerting and arrives with a superior finishing kick; Good ground and a fair gallop suit a horse that travels well into a race rather than making it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Arrives In Time
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and strings out the field, allowing the deeper closers to pick through.
scenarios.body: A horse like Minella Buoy or Sofi's Gift, slipping through gaps from a true hold-up position, gets a dream run to the last and finishes strongest of all; this scenario is discounted because most natural hold-up types are mapped out of their preferred role and face traffic in a compacted midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 13-runner field causes interference, horses lose their positions and the race develops a scrappy, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: Unexpected pace injections from jostling midfielders disrupt Words Unspoken's rhythm and the race becomes messy, creating a lottery that benefits a fresh or unexposed runner; Camp Verde or Motherland, both lightly raced and open to improvement, could capitalise on the unpredictability.

watchPoints.text: Words Unspoken sets the only confirmed pace — if Enright is allowed to dictate unopposed, the race shape collapses into a procession that is very hard for the field to reverse from the final hurdle.

Nicky Larson is the only prominent type likely to track the leader, meaning its decision to push on or sit tight from the second-last could prove decisive for any horse relying on cover in the chasing pack.

Minella Buoy and Sofi's Gift both have the most relevant hurdles form for the distance but their hold-up styles will be compromised by the 13-runner field — monitor whether either can find a clear passage around the home turn.

Motherland and Camp Verde are both unknown quantities making early hurdling appearances for significant stables — either could be significantly ahead of their market position if lightly-raced flat form has been withheld.

No Bother Aoife wears a tongue-tie and has been consistent at the trip; Cromwell's 14-day record of one from 29 is modest, but the horse's form profile over 17f on Good is the most course-and-distance relevant among the deeper hold-up types.

races.name: Bank Of Ireland Brendan Maloney Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Cummins Homevalue Hardware Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Long Gone
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with solid Good-ground credentials — sim-going record of 3W6P is strong — but 57 days off and a visor fitted raises a small query; needs a stronger gallop than this field is likely to produce to deliver from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Long Gone showed smart form when winning four starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is her two pulled-up efforts in between, plus 57 days off, mean confidence in her bouncing back cannot be total.

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning on 25 days rest for a trainer in decent recent form; 10th on his Good-ground reappearance last time is concerning, and the compressed midfield this race shape creates makes his task harder than his form suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Secret Rock returns after 25 days carrying 161 lb, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour — though he'll need to bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type whose sole win came over the same 16f trip on Good, so the extra yardage here is untested; the apprentice claim (5lb) from Kenneally is useful but his trainer has no runners in the past 14 days, which is worth flagging in a tactical race.
runners_data.comment: Figero landed a win two starts back but has been unplaced in three of his last five, and our rating of 92 trails his official mark of 103, suggesting he may be working off a flattering handicap weight. Has run over today's trip and going, though a fifth last time out leaves him needing to find more.

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who should slot comfortably behind Ripsnorter — the natural second slot is his for the taking; zero wins from nine Good-ground starts is a concern, and four days since last run on a big field card is tight, though O'Sullivan's horses are fit to run frequently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn from a struggling yard that has gone 0/27 in the past fortnight, Go To Town faces an uphill task at 155 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 101 offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, and Danny Mullins can dictate entirely on his own terms; form line of 310 includes a win and a third over similar distances on Good, though the step back up after a 7th and 6th in recent runs needs explaining.
runners_data.comment: Ripsnorter won four starts back and was third five starts back, giving him some form to point to, yet three consecutive unplaced efforts since cloud his claims; he has run over today's trip and going, and 155 lb is no gimme at OR 99.

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: A 4yo with a tendency to race handy (trainer angle via McNiff); runs in hood, which could sharpen his jumping, and his one win came on Good at 16f — this 2m½f trip is the longest he has attempted, which is a genuine stamina query.
runners_data.comment: Houndsworth won four starts back but has struggled for consistency since, finishing out of the frame in his last three outings; he has run over today's trip and going, yet 154 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated 101 officially.

runners_data.name: Fremantle Doctor
runners_data.note: 161 days off the track is a significant flag — despite being a hold-up horse at heart with two placed efforts from seven Good-ground runs, the long absence combined with the race shape offering little late pace to close into makes his position awkward; trainer McConnell is 2/29 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Ran third three starts back but winless in his last four, Fremantle Doctor brings useful form to this contest and our rating of 103 has him right in the mix; the concern is a 161-day absence carrying 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type who sits nearer the rear in his own races, but the single front-runner here means he will be shunted into a midfield he doesn't naturally inhabit; his 13 Good-ground runs producing 1W3P show he handles conditions, yet racing out of role blunts his finishing prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Le Diablo does at least bring placings — third and second in consecutive runs two and three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before, but 152 lb is a stern burden and his trainer is without a strike in 24 runners over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Atlantic Gamble
runners_data.note: 76 days off and a record that reads 0W0P from 15 Good-ground runs tells its own story — a hold-up horse who hasn't converted on this surface, and forced into an unnatural midfield position, this is a race where his strengths are least likely to be exposed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Atlantic Gamble hasn't troubled the judge recently, and 76 days off the track does little to inspire confidence — ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here, despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Final Decision
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who posted 2nd and 6th in similar contests and whose trainer Rothwell has two winners from 23 runners in the past fortnight — a live each-way profile if he can sit second or third and produce a clean jumping round; 86 days since last run is the main doubt.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts and returning after 86 days off, Final Decision does at least have experience over today's trip and conditions — though her recent unplaced efforts and that fall give pause, and 151 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Koeur A Prendre
runners_data.note: Back-to-back seconds in his last two runs over 20f on Good are eye-catching — a genuinely in-form stayer — but his natural hold-up style will be frustrated by the race shape, and he will need fortune in running to thread through a compressed rear division.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with two seconds his best recent efforts, Koeur A Prendre ranks 11th of 14 on our figures and carries 150 lb, making him hard to fancy; experience of today's going is the one positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Brave Crogha
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up operator whose entire sim-going record (1W2P from 13) is workmanlike at best on Good; the visor is retained but form figures of 0909P give limited confidence, and this race shape is actively unhelpful for a horse who needs a strongly run race to reach his rivals.
runners_data.comment: Ranked third of 14 on our ratings, Brave Crogha has run over today's trip and going and shaped with more promise than his bare figures suggest — the chief concern is a pulled-up effort most recently and 76 days off the track since.

runners_data.name: Theanniversary Man
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back hurdles (1/20f HEA, 1/16f GOO) showing he can finish well off a pace; however, he is a natural hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield — in a race with a single relaxed pace-setter — means he is unlikely to generate the late momentum those wins required.

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Solid each-way form including 2nd at 22f on Soft and a win at 19f on Good — trainer McKiernan is in form with 2 winners from 8 runs; a hold-up horse by nature yet compact enough in style that he could be one of the more dangerous of the redistributed group if he finds clear daylight at the second-last.
runners_data.comment: Chemdawg has shown she can win in recent starts — a winner two starts back, and second last time out — but she has pulled up twice in her last five and our rating ranks her last of the fourteen here, making her very hard to fancy despite the distance and going experience.

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — Danny Mullins should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 2m½f Ballinrobe hurdle on Good ground. The prominent types Go To Town and Final Decision will track close but neither is a natural front-runner, meaning Ripsnorter sets the terms without the kind of pressure that would blow the race apart early. This is a single-pace scenario where the leader can conserve energy, jump fluently and ask questions of closers at the second-last — a shape that historically rewards those who travel smoothly in the first two or three off the pace rather than those forced to make up ground late. Fremantle Doctor, Le Diablo, Atlantic Gamble, Koeur A Prendre, Brave Crogha, Theanniversary Man and Chemdawg are all genuine hold-up horses that cannot all find their natural position at the rear with only one true front-runner to follow; Ripsnorter and the nearest trackers Go To Town and Final Decision are the likeliest to secure their preferred spots, compressing the true hold-up brigade into an awkward midfield mass. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently or in the first third off Ripsnorter's controlled pace, travel into the race without burning fuel, and produce a jump-and-gallop finish — not horses relying on a strong pace to collapse and let them close from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Leads, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter sets a fair but not excessive gallop and the nearest prominent trackers travel well throughout.
scenarios.body: Ripsnorter controls the tempo from the front and the race develops into a jumping test from three out, with Go To Town and Final Decision poised to challenge as the field strings out; the measured early pace means those in the first four who have saved their energy hold the upper hand on the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter is allowed an uncontested, notably slow early pace and builds enough of a lead that the field cannot reel him in.
scenarios.body: Danny Mullins exploits the total absence of pace pressure to dictate a bouncing, confidence-boosting gallop, and Ripsnorter's 5yo freshness on Good ground allows him to find enough in reserve from the last hurdle; those further back simply have too much to do if the gap has opened at the top of the home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Surge Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If a pocket of the redistibuted midfield horses — Le Diablo or Chemdawg — move early to improve position, injecting pace into the middle of the race and stringing things out.
scenarios.body: The premature move turns the race into a slog from well out, punishing those who have already used energy settling in the compressed midfield; horses with proven stamina and a willingness to battle — Chemdawg and Koeur A Prendre — would be better placed than those needing a true sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter's early tempo is fractionally quicker than it appears and the field is genuinely strung out by halfway, leaving true hold-up horses with a fast-run race to close into.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong-run race would bring the hold-up horses back into play, but the structural problem is that most of them are compressed into a traffic-heavy midfield rather than tracking cleanly off the pace; only Figero or Long Gone, who show good form on Good ground with finishing kicks in similar conditions, could realistically thread through.

watchPoints.text: Ripsnorter (Danny Mullins) — watch whether he goes off at a crawl or a fair clip; if Mullins dawdles in front, the entire race shape compresses and those sitting closest at halfway rather than furthest back become the main beneficiaries.

Go To Town — returned just four days ago and runs again here; if Eoin Staples pushes forward immediately to claim second spot, he sets the primary challenge to Ripsnorter, but any signs of tiredness after a recent run would expose the dangers of quick back-up in a 14-runner field.

Le Diablo — J J Slevin is a top jockey capable of improvising when a horse is out of its natural position; watch whether Slevin opts to push forward from the off to grab a better pitch rather than sitting where the pace map places him, which could inject a surprise mid-race surge.

Chemdawg (Phillip Enright, McKiernan yard 2/8 T14) — the in-form yard combination is worth monitoring in-running; if Enright gets a clear run from the back of the midfield bunch from three out, Chemdawg's staying form on Good is good enough to threaten the lead group late.

Koeur A Prendre — two consecutive runner-up efforts in recent starts suggest a horse in the form of his life; watch his position at halfway, as Daniel King will need to be creative threading through traffic for any repeat of those placed runs to materialise from this race shape.

races.name: Broderick's Electric Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Grey Gardens
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old trained by Paul Nolan; has placed twice in similar going across five starts on Good, and Eoin Staples (5lb claimer) provides a weight advantage that matters at OR 98 in a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Grey Gardens arrives with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating places him top of a 19-runner field — a strong claim for favouritism. Third three starts back and fourth last time, he's winless in recent starts, and 38 days off is the query.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: J J Slevin aboard this hold-up six-year-old but a persistent pattern of fading late — seen in all recent Good-ground efforts — is a serious concern over this trip; no wins or places from six Good-ground runs.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 19 here, Home By The Sea does have experience over today's trip and going, but a burden of 167 lb makes life hard for a gelding who has managed just a fourth and a fifth in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Let Him B
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a win and a place on Good ground; the 74-day break and a fade warning noted, but has won over 20f on Good and the extra distance suits if fit.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a second three starts back and won four starts back, but two unplaced runs since leave him needing to bounce back after 74 days off; he has run over today's trip and the 165 lb burden is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse with three Good-ground places in the last 15 attempts; the headgear flag (tongue tie) is noted, and an unseated last time adds a question mark, but has placed at 2m6f+ previously.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in recent starts, The Vegas Raider nonetheless showed promise with a second three starts back, though an unseated last time and a hefty 163 lb to carry are the checks on his claims; experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old for Thomas Mullins ridden by Danny Mullins; ran only seven days ago which raises freshness concerns, and fades late regularly, but has won on Good ground and the stable/jockey combination commands respect.|
runners_data.comment: Scrambled back to winning ways two starts back but has looked below that level since, finishing unplaced last time out; he has run over today's distance and going before, though 161 lb is a stiff ask for one ranked seventh of nineteen.

runners_data.name: Cool Summer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up mare who finds herself mapped to midfield because the field is overloaded with rear-runners; has two places from ten Good-ground starts and headgear (hood) suggests she needs help to concentrate.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out after a string of moderate efforts, Cool Summer arrives here 35 days on with experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour — winless in her last five, but that runner-up showing and a rating of 93 make her a tempting each-way proposition under 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Euro Maker
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by profile pushed forward on the map due to redistribution; the fade warning and 75-day absence are notable negatives, though placed second on Good ground at 2m in recent form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 19 on our figures, Euro Maker also pulled up three starts back and has 75 days off as a fitness concern; has run over today's trip and going, but a ninth last time out makes him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up ten-year-old with a strong Good-ground record (five places including wins across 15 attempts); 246-day layoff is the critical unknown, and though mapped to midfield here, naturally wants to come from behind.|
runners_data.comment: Sayitfirst has consecutive seconds in her recent record and a win before that, showing she can mix it at this level, and has run over today's trip and going — our rating of 95 puts her right in the mix; the risk is that pulled-up run on return from 246 days off.

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with John Joseph Hanlon's yard in form (1/15 T14), she runs from behind by inclination and is slotted to midfield on the map against her nature; no wins on Good ground in nine attempts is damning.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Victoria Kesia does at least return third three starts back to show she can find the frame, and she has run over today's trip and going before; however, carrying 156 lb looks a stiff ask for a mare rated 87.

runners_data.name: The Toothpicker
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and the key pace-setter in this race; has finished fifth five consecutive times which screams consistency without a killer finish, and at OR 86 the question is whether a sole leader can hold on over 2m½f against a chasing pack.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 108 days off the track, The Toothpicker arrives short of recent encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 91 gives him a sliver of upside at 155 lb.

runners_data.name: All In Peder
runners_data.note: Mapped to midfield but a natural hold-up horse; two wins and three places from 15 Good-ground runs look encouraging on paper, though recent form shows P-0-0 pattern and the lengthy AW-free runs at Ballinrobe suggest modest current form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up three runs back, All In Peder arrives on a retrieval mission; he has run over today's trip and going, but carrying 153 lb as an 11th-ranked runner makes progression a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Spread The Faith
runners_data.note: Oliver McKiernan-trained hold-up type naturally displaced into midfield on the map; the fade flag and three pulled-up runs in recent form are alarming, though did manage fourth last time and trainer is 2/8 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts — including three pull-ups — and ranked well adrift on our figures, Spread The Faith faces a stiff ask here; a return to today's trip and going at least offers familiar conditions, but 81 days off and 150 lb make this hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Lunar Landscape
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old mapped forward due to overcrowding at the rear; best form on Good ground but has finished 6th-13th in recent attempts, and a 31-day break provides reasonable freshness without strong handicap case.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 17th of 19 on our figures, Lunar Landscape is hard to fancy here; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a 148 lb burden makes life even tougher.

runners_data.name: Sidiriya
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell yard in decent form (2/23 T14); a natural hold-up type now mapped slightly forward, has placed twice from 15 Good-ground starts and a consistent 2nd-3rd-5th sequence in recent runs shows genuine competitiveness.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 19 on our figures, Sidiriya faces a stiff ask under 145 lb, though second and third finishes two and three starts back show she can get competitive — and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bangor Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old with a fade tendency mapped to midfield; no wins or places from eight Good-ground starts tells a bleak story for this surface, and the 17-day turnaround adds workload pressure.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a fall — and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Bangor Lady faces an uphill task, with a trainer who has gone 0/24 in the last 14 days adding little confidence; experience over today's trip and going is the one small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Western Doyen
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old veteran returning from 643 days off — that layoff is extraordinary and must dominate any assessment; maps as prominent which makes him one of only two horses likely to actually sit near The Toothpicker, but fitness after nearly two years away is wholly unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up last time out, Western Doyen returns after a 643-day absence — a huge ask at this level — though he has run over today's distance and going before, and a second two starts back offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Calm Flight Ahead
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old mapped to midfield against natural inclination; only one run on Good ground from five starts, the fade flag is present, and a sequence of six consecutive tailed-off or pulled-up efforts makes this a significant risk.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out and winless in his last five starts, Calm Flight Ahead returns after 74 days off carrying 148 lb; he's lightly raced and unexposed enough to leave that latest effort behind.

runners_data.name: Ikalimix
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse without a declared jockey listed; recent fall last time out raises jumping concerns, and a tongue-tie is noted — has placed once on Good ground but form trajectory is poor.|
runners_data.comment: Ikalimix lines up just seven days after his last outing, and having run over today's trip and going, he arrives with strong claims — our rating has him second of 19. The fall in his most recent start is the obvious concern for a horse winless in his last four.

runners_data.name: Moulane West
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran hold-up type — naturally wants to race from the rear but is displaced into midfield on the map by the volume of rear-runners; tongue-tie worn, ran only four days ago which is a genuine freshness concern despite a win and two places on Good ground.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and stepping back out just four days after his latest unplaced effort, Moulane West faces a stiff ask under 157 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, though a rating of 90 suggests he holds his own in this field.

races.paceDynamic: The Toothpicker is the only confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, with no other genuine pace horse pressing it, should dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Western Doyen, mapped as prominent, may try to track but neither that horse nor anything else appears likely to seriously challenge The Toothpicker for the early lead, meaning the pace will be honest but not searching. A lone, uncontested leader setting a measured gallop over 2m½f on Good turf strongly favours closers who travel well through midfield and have the ability to quicken from off the pace, as the lack of genuine pressure typically compresses the field and rewards those who save their energy. This field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Moulane West, Victoria Kesia, Sayitfirst, Cool Summer and others are genuine forward-racing horses who will be squeezed into midfield positions against their will; The Toothpicker and Western Doyen are the only runners realistically able to secure forward berths from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Toothpicker Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If The Toothpicker leads throughout at a controlled pace and no rival has the tactical speed to reel it in.
scenarios.body: The Toothpicker sets a sustainable tempo from the front, and horses tracking just off the pace through the middle stages have time to organise and quicken; the absence of a pressing rival means the leader is fresh enough at the last to resist or only just be caught.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is just fast enough in the final mile to take the edge off The Toothpicker, allowing strong-finishing hold-up types to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace tightens the field entering the home straight, but The Toothpicker's reserves are spent once challenged at the last hurdle, and horses who travelled smoothly in mid-division deliver a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Western Doyen or a remapped prominent type manages to press The Toothpicker and a front-two gallop develops.
scenarios.body: A genuine two-horse pace develops making it a stiffer test of stamina throughout, suiting horses with proven staying power at the trip who can sit just behind and pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Reshuffle Scrambles Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field sees significant early positional battles among redistributed horses forcing an uneven, stop-start tempo.
scenarios.body: Horses who are adaptable mid-to-rear types and avoid trouble in traffic benefit most as the field strings out unpredictably; those forced wide or into unexpected positions early are compromised.

watchPoints.text: The Toothpicker's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — watch whether any runner breaks sharply enough at the start to press it early, as that would fundamentally alter the pace shape and compress the entire field.|

Sayitfirst returns from 246 days off; if it shows pre-race signs of sharpness and travels fluidly in the early stages, the Good-ground record (5 places, 1 win from 15) makes it one of the most dangerous horses in the race despite the layoff.|

Western Doyen is 643 days absent and at 13 years old; watch for any physical signs at the start, as a horse at this age returning from nearly two years off could set a false pace or cause disruption if it struggles to fill its natural prominent role.|

With 19 runners and the vast majority wanting to come from behind, watch for significant traffic trouble in the straight — horses like Grey Gardens, Max Meridius and Sidiriya could all be boxed in or forced wide as the field fans out after the last.|

Trainer P J Rothwell has two runners (Sidiriya and Calm Flight Ahead) and is 2/23 over 14 days — Sidiriya is the obvious stable representative with recent form, but monitor declarations or market moves for any stable-runner preference signal.|

races.name: Burleigh Accountancy Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Poor recent form string (8560-0) with zero wins or places on similar going across five runs; the extra 3m2f trip at Ballinrobe is the one potential positive angle, but the evidence for a revival is thin at OR 116.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, My Trump Card nevertheless holds the strongest rating in the field and has run over today's trip before; carrying 166 lb is the concern, but he is fresh on just eight days' rest and demands respect.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with genuine placed form on Good ground (0W2P in four similar-going runs), a 5lb claimer in the saddle cutting the weight, and a trainer who has fired one winner from 15 recent runners; hold-up style suits if pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Killowen House showed his class with a win in his last five starts and ran a solid third two starts back, so the zip is there — today's going holds no fears, and 12 days between runs suggests freshness. The weight of 161 lb is the one factor to navigate.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record (13 runs, 1W5P) and a tongue-piece fitted, but this confirmed sit-and-wait type is pushed forward into midfield by the volume of hold-up horses in the field — his chance is tempered by the race not playing to his hands.
runners_data.comment: Dorans Law ran a bold race to finish second last time out and, ranked second in the field on our ratings, he shapes as a serious threat here; winless in his last five starts, however, he must prove he can convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Form figures (76-867) tell a stark story with limited upside; another natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield positions by the field's composition, and no wins or places on Good ground across 10 qualifying runs make it difficult to be positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lord Ffrench nevertheless has experience of today's going and arrives fresh on just 12 days' rest, with our rating of 110 marking him out as a live contender — the concern is that his recent string of back-of-field finishes offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and the key pace-setter; returning from 87 days off, which is a notable absence, and has no wins on Good ground from four similar-going runs — but his tactical control of this race from the front is undeniable regardless of ability.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Strange Currency faces a stiff task here; 87 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's going before and that counts for something.

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained nine-year-old with solid Good-ground form (1W4P in 13 similar runs), a blinkered headgear note to sharpen focus, and a prominent style that keeps him in the race regardless of what Strange Currency does up front; the 31-day break is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a third three starts back and a runner-up four starts back hinting at ability he hasn't lately reproduced; a trainer firing at just 4% adds concern, though going experience and an 11-point ratings edge over his mark offer some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form (57-324) with placed efforts on Good ground and a horse who has finished second and third in recent outings; ran just 4 days ago which is a significant freshness concern, and his natural hold-up style is compromised by the field shape — still the most likely of the redistributed trio to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Run For The Border faces a stiff ask here — a return just four days ago adds to the concern, and her trainer is without a winner in 24 attempts over the past fortnight. Going experience at least offers some consolation.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old with excellent Good-ground profile (14 runs, 1W7P), a tongue-tie fitted, and a prominent racing style that places him perfectly just behind Strange Currency — one of the better-suited horses to a controlled-tempo shape over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but showed a return to form with a third last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 142 lb looks the stiffest hurdle for a mare rated 104 by us yet to fully convert her ability.

races.paceDynamic: Strange Currency is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m2f handicap hurdle and will dictate matters from the front on Good ground at Ballinrobe, setting a controlled, manageable tempo with no genuine rival to pressure or push the pace from the flag. Down Around and Ladiam will look to sit prominently just behind, meaning the early sections will not be truly contested and Strange Currency can conserve energy through the long middle portions of the trip. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Dorans Law, Lord Ffrench, and Run For The Border are all genuine sit-and-wait horses who will be forced to operate closer to midfield than their natural position through sheer weight of numbers, meaning their reliance on a strong pace to close into is undermined from the outset. This race shape — a lone leader setting a fair but uncontested gallop over 3m2f on Good ground — strongly favours horses with the stamina to travel prominently or just off the pace and outstay rivals in the straight, rather than true closers who need a searching tempo to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strange Currency Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Strange Currency bowls along at his own unhurried pace and the hold-up horses, forced into midfield, never generate sufficient momentum to close.
scenarios.body: Strange Currency dictates every yard, dictates the tempo, and with no rival willing or able to press him, he rations his effort before quickening away from the second-last flight; Down Around and Ladiam, sitting closest, are best placed of the chasers but face a gap already opened.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind Him Down
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around or Ladiam apply enough sustained pressure from two out to wear down Strange Currency before the last.
scenarios.body: The pace proves just honest enough over 3m2f that the leader begins to weaken approaching the final flight, and a relentlessly travelling Down Around or Ladiam — who both handle Good ground well — arrive to collar him close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find A Way Through
scenarios.trigger: If Strange Currency sets a fast enough gallop that the genuine hold-up horses — despite being pushed forward — can still make telling late ground.
scenarios.body: Run For The Border, who has shown consistent form at this trip on Good ground with good recent figures, produces a sustained late run if the pace has been true enough to create gaps; Dorans Law, with strong Good-ground credentials and a tongue-tie, could also arrive late if stamina tests the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Outsider Profits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments mid-race through jumping errors or crowding, creating an unusual tactical situation that suits an unexpected profiler.
scenarios.body: Killowen House, lightly raced at 6 with good recent placed form on Good ground and a 5lb claimer in the saddle, could benefit from a messy race if those ahead are checked or unseated; My Trump Card's strong track-and-trip record at Ballinrobe on Good gives a slender each-way foothold.

watchPoints.text: Strange Currency has been off 87 days — watch his jumping early; any mistakes at the first two flights under Philip Byrnes could shatter his controlled front-running plan entirely.
Run For The Border ran just 4 days ago and faces a significant stamina test at 3m2f; monitor his travelling in the back straight as fatigue from a quick turnaround could surface before the home turn.

Dorans Law, Lord Ffrench, and Run For The Border are all forced closer to midfield than they naturally want to be — if they bunch together on the inner around the final bend, traffic trouble is a real risk for all three.

Down Around's application of blinkers is worth tracking through the race; if the headgear sharpens his jumping and he travels sweetly behind Strange Currency, he becomes the most dangerous chaser in the field.

races.name: Bay Leaf Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Barton Sky
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon handler, 17 days since last run; form shows only minor placings at best and true rearward style means this horse will struggle to exert influence in a race lacking genuine pace — naturally a hold-up runner working wider than ideal.

runners_data.name: Boomerang Breeze
runners_data.note: Fades in finish flag is a significant concern over 2m6½f on Good ground; Timothy Doyle's charge is a true hold-up type who cannot get to the rear in this crowded field, reducing their chance further in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Derby Rock
runners_data.note: James Kieran King-trained 7yo with a modest form string including a fall; runs from a hold-up position naturally but the combination of amateur jockey Mr P A King (3) and a crowded field makes finding clear daylight at the finish difficult.

runners_data.name: Gainsville
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead stable in decent form (T14: 4/35) and Darragh O'Keeffe is a top booking; unknown style (U) means tactical flexibility could be an asset, and De Bromhead's horses often travel well, making a prominent-to-tracking position plausible over a staying trip.

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a strong jockey booking for Peter Maher; genuine hold-up style compressed into midfield here, and with a form line of 26-376 showing no wins, the lack of a true closing gallop is a structural problem.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: Danny Gilligan rides for Cian Collins; prominent style (P) makes this horse ideally placed to track Go To The Moon in a race with little other genuine pace — the natural position at the head of the chasing group is a real tactical edge at 2m6½f.

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Only 6 days since last run (quick turnaround to note); Alan O'Sullivan (5) takes the ride for David Barry and this horse's true hold-up tendency is masked by the redistribution — freshness from the recent run is a marginal positive but the style conflict remains the key issue.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright partners Edward Power's 5yo who carries a fades-in-finish warning; form of 76-060 is uninspiring and the hold-up tendency means Rumi Rock needs things to go wrong for rivals rather than doing anything of its own accord.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell sends out this 5yo with Tiernan Power Roche aboard; the form includes a win (/P1) which is notable, and although a hold-up type, the 65-day break could see the horse come fresh and travel well enough to be involved late in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Brian Mortell runner with amateur Conor Smithers (7) up; fades-in-finish flag combined with a hold-up style and redistribution out of natural position makes this one of the most structurally disadvantaged runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Likeyouhaveplenty
runners_data.note: Sean O'Brien handler, 35 days between runs; form of P-00 with a fades-in-finish flag tells a consistent story of promise not converted, and the hold-up style offers little hope in a race lacking the searching gallop needed to bring closers into play.

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins is always a significant trainer flag (T14: 18/65) and Brian Hayes is a quality jockey; limited form (6-9) but the stable's ability to improve horses quickly cannot be dismissed, and a hold-up type in a Mullins yard often races more prominently than their label suggests.

runners_data.name: Secret Moon
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon fields this lightly raced 5yo with Josh Younge; fades-in-finish and unknown style flags create uncertainty, and the form of 688 over shorter trips leaves a genuine stamina question over 2m6½f.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan has a quiet recent record (T14: 0/27) and Shane Markey (7) takes the ride; the fades-in-finish flag is a recurring theme and a distance of 2m6½f looks against this horse based on finishing patterns in shorter company.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends Jack Kennedy — a very strong jockey appointment — aboard this progressive 5yo whose form of 556 shows consistent placed efforts; a hold-up type who has run into Good ground consistently and whose trainer's runners are always fit, making this one of the more interesting structured runners despite redistribution.

runners_data.name: Go To The Moon
runners_data.note: Mark McNiff's 6yo is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting they may not be a natural leader; nevertheless with no rival to press them they will control the tempo over 2m6½f on Good ground, and the big question is whether they can maintain that advantage into the home straight.

races.paceDynamic: Go To The Moon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse maiden hurdle over 2m6½f at Ballinrobe on Good ground, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, they are set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a lone leader with no pressure will naturally settle into a rhythm that keeps the race together until the home straight, making this a test of jumping accuracy and staying power rather than raw speed. This shape most clearly favours prominent racers and those who can track the leader in the first few behind, able to pounce when the tempo lifts late, rather than true hold-up horses who need a searching gallop to close ground. Several runners in this field — Kilmond Knight, Hey Sir, Boomerang Breeze, Barton Sky, and others — are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because the field is saturated with rear-of-field profiles; of those, Keep Em Quite and Gainsville are best placed to naturally secure a prominent or tracking position, giving them a structural advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Go To The Moon sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking the pace from the second or third flight.
scenarios.body: Go To The Moon bowls along at a comfortable clip, keeping the field bunched and setting up a stamina-based finish from the home turn; horses within three lengths of the leader turning in have a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Go To The Moon's controlled pace is so moderate that they conserve enough energy to outstay all rivals up the home straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival able to mount a sustained challenge from off the pace over this trip, Go To The Moon's jumping and front-running experience prove decisive; the race becomes a procession in the final half mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and a horse from mid-division produces a sharp turn of foot in the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: A bunched, processional gallop results in a sprint finish where agility and freshness matter more than position; a horse settled just off midfield with a clear run can thread through tired rivals late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong or the field strings out, allowing one of the genuine closers to pick off tiring rivals in the final flight.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because the field's true hold-up types — Barton Sky, Boomerang Breeze, Hey Sir — are forced out of role and are unlikely to be racing from their natural position; any late thrust depends on an uncharacteristically honest gallop.

watchPoints.text: Go To The Moon controls all tempo — if they find a comfortable rhythm and jump well, no rival is structurally positioned to force a change in pace, handing them a significant race-shape advantage.

Keep Em Quite is the only confirmed prominent-style (P) runner outside the front-runner and Danny Gilligan should be able to slot into second or third early — watch how quickly they move up from the off, as that position could be pivotal.

Room For One More represents the Willie Mullins/Jack Kennedy-calibre angle (Hayes aboard) and despite limited form, Mullins runners in maiden hurdles often outrun their bare form — watch for a prominent move from the back two hurdles out.

With so many hold-up types redistributed to midfield, the middle stages are likely to be congested — watch for traffic trouble turning in, particularly affecting Hey Sir, Kilmond Knight, and Barton Sky if any late pace develops.

Western Shores (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) has shown consistent form and the jockey booking is high quality for what looks a routine maiden; watch whether Kennedy rides prominently despite the hold-up style tag, which Elliott's runners sometimes do in small-field scenarios.

races.name: Tim Kelly Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Phillip Enright; won over this course and distance on Good going and has strong place form in similar conditions, making it one of the more credible closers if the pace is honest enough to suit.
runners_data.comment: Nothing Hectic does bring a win four starts back and distance-and-going experience to the table, and her official mark of 98 suggests she retains ability; the chief concern is that her last three runs have been deeply disappointing, capped by a pull-up.

runners_data.name: Cornaroya Rocco
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle is a significant booking; a hold-up horse who has placed at this trip on Good ground before, though his form has been patchy and stepping back up in distance requires some confidence.
runners_data.comment: Finished second last time out and returns on going he has experienced before, Cornaroya Rocco arrives here 25 days later in reasonable order; winless in his last five starts, but that recent runner-up effort keeps him interesting at 167 lb off an official mark of 97.

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: 440 days off the track is a significant concern for Barry Connell's five-year-old; won over this trip on Good going before the break and the fading-in-finish flag suggests stamina may not be as reliable as the win suggested — freshness is a double-edged sword here.
runners_data.comment: Tannery Park won last time out but that came 440 days ago, making his return from a lengthy absence the key question; he has run over today's trip and going before, though our rating of 89 leaves him needing to find improvement on recent form against this field.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old running just two days after his last start, which is an unusual pattern; has placed twice at 25f on Good going recently but the hold-up style and age make him vulnerable in a big field where positioning is everything.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in his last two starts, The Little Yank arrives here just two days on from his latest effort and has run over today's trip and conditions before — our rating of 96 makes him the one to beat among 19 rivals, though that quick turnaround and a hefty 163 lb could test his stamina.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Four-year-old on just a 56-day break, hurdling experience limited but did place at 24f on Good going; headgear noted and the fading-in-finish flag raises questions about whether he truly stays this 2m6½f trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 11th of 19 on our rating, Pilgrims Walk does bring going experience and a second last time out to the table, though 56 days off and a hefty 162 lb in the weights are the clear concerns here.

runners_data.name: Political Stance
runners_data.note: 146-day absence and a modest form string over shorter trips; has placed on Heavy going but the record on Good is thin, and the hold-up style in this big field with no searching pace is a compounding disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts and returning from a 146-day absence after being pulled up last time, Political Stance faces questions on fitness; he has run over today's going before, though the hefty 161 lb burden will test him further.

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: One of the genuine prominent types in the race who should actually get that position; a 10-year-old but active, and headgear noted — has won on Good ground and the track record at this sort of trip is solid enough to make him a legitimate pace-shape beneficiary.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and carrying a hefty 160 lb, It's Time Again has a patchy recent record — a fall and a pull-up among them — though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a handy 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes over on this 10-year-old prominent racer, which is a notable jockey upgrade; placed at 22f on Good recently and, crucially, is one of the few who should genuinely sit close to Joshua Chamberlain rather than being shuffled back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up three times in that spell, Ranger Billy arrives with obvious questions to answer; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out at least shows some residual ability, though 155 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who is mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is overcrowded — form at 20f on Good is poor and the style-fit discount is warranted; Andrew Slattery's 3/38 trainer strike-rate in the last 14 days is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Poetic Focus has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a burden of 154 lb makes the task tougher, and her recent sequence — including a fall — offers limited encouragement despite a rating of 86 suggesting some residual ability.

runners_data.name: Chanceitlucky
runners_data.note: 267 days off the course is a significant flag; a true hold-up horse squeezed into midfield on the map, carries the fading-in-finish concern too, and there is nothing in the recent form to suggest this layoff has been used productively.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning from a 267-day absence, Chanceitlucky faces a stiff ask here — our rating of 64 ranks him 17th of 19 — and carrying 152 lb only compounds the concern; the fourth two starts back is the sole flicker of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Moonshine Girl
runners_data.note: Has finished second twice in recent starts, including at 24f on Good, and is one of the more honest hold-up types in the race; mapped to midfield through congestion rather than style change, but those placings suggest she can finish through horses if any pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a pulled-up effort mixed into that sequence, Moonshine Girl has shown placings two starts back and last time out but is ranked 14th of 19 on our figures and carries a hefty 150 lb — hard to fancy despite the distance and going experience.

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a poor record on Good ground (2 from 6 in sim-going), headgear worn, fading-in-finish flag and a natural hold-up style pushed further up the map than is natural — multiple negatives stack up here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 89 days off, Urbs Intacta Manet is lightly raced enough to leave room for progress, and the unexposed profile makes him one to monitor as he rounds into form under 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Mini Getaway
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at this sort of trip on various going, including 24f on Good; a genuine prominent-style runner who should get his position and Alex Harvey knows the horse — one of the more likely horses to sit close to the pace and run an honest race.
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner three starts back and was third last time out, but 94 days off the track is a notable concern; she has experience over today's trip and going, though a rating of 77 leaves her with plenty to find against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: Four runs in the data, all on Good or near-Good, and all finishing outside the top ten; hold-up style crammed into midfield, fading-in-finish flag, and just 17 days since last run — insufficient reason to be confident here.
runners_data.comment: Tawny Lea arrives here just 17 days since her last outing, yet remains unexposed and open to improvement; she is yet to win in recent starts, though her lightly raced profile suggests there could be more to come under her 148 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Queen Kulina
runners_data.note: 10-year-old prominent racer who has placed three times at 24f on Good, giving her solid course-and-distance profile credentials; Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim is useful in a big-field handicap and she should get a handy berth.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a fall and two eighths among her recent figures, Queen Kulina faces a stiff ask ranked 15 of 19 on our assessment; she has run over today's trip and going, and a third two starts back offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: La Tene
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 22f on Good going and has shown some consistency; mapped to midfield rather than rear because the hold-up section is overcrowded, and the style-fit score of 0.93 suggests the positional compromise is modest — worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 19 on our figures, La Tene is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a respectable 20-day break; two falls or exits in that sequence make jumping reliability a real concern.

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is a practical concern; form reads 9-98P5 and the fades-in-finish flag alongside a poor Good-going record (0 wins from 9 sim-going runs) leaves very little to work with positively.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up among them, Lost Features arrives carrying 144 lb ranked 16 of 19 on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, but there is precious little in her recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Everystep Oftheway
runners_data.note: 763 days off the track is the headline fact — that is over two years; despite consistently placing at 24-25f on Good in its prime, this kind of absence with no jockey listed makes it almost impossible to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for over two years, Everystep Oftheway faces questions about fitness, though his experience on today's going and a rating of 88 offer some encouragement; fourth four times in recent starts shows consistency without the cutting edge to match it.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner who will dictate this race from the front; the style-fit flag at 0.90 reflects that he is not a habitual leader but the race conditions make him one by default — his ability to control fractions completely is the single biggest tactical factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Joshua Chamberlain has run over today's trip and going, arrives in good order on 20 days' rest, and a win four starts back gives his recent form real substance — the risk is that his last two outings, a fourth and an unplaced run, suggest he needs to find a bit more.

races.paceDynamic: Joshua Chamberlain is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press him, he is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop over the 2m6½f trip on Good ground. The remainder of the field is stacked with hold-up types — Poetic Focus, Everystep Oftheway, Chanceitlucky, Moonshine Girl, La Tene and several others are all natural hold-up horses but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field simply cannot accommodate them all. The horses most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind Joshua Chamberlain are It's Time Again, Ranger Billy, Mini Getaway and Queen Kulina, who are the genuine P-style runners in this race. With one-paced, sustainable fractions expected and a field of 19 grinding out 2m6½f on good ground, this race shape strongly favours resolute, prominent-racing types who can sit close to Joshua Chamberlain and pounce from a handy position, rather than true hold-up horses whose finishing kicks will be blunted by the absence of a genuine searching pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Joshua Chamberlain dictates a modest, uncontested gallop and the race lacks the pressure needed to bring hold-up horses into play.
scenarios.body: Joshua Chamberlain sets fractions entirely on his own terms, with It's Time Again and Ranger Billy tracking in behind and the hold-up pack stranded too far back to reel them in. Prominent types who save ground around the flat, turning track at Ballinrobe and travel well into the straight hold a decisive positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Joshua Chamberlain's uncontested lead translates into enough energy saved that he holds on into the finish.
scenarios.body: Without any pace pressure, Joshua Chamberlain essentially controls his own tempo and could arrive at the last flight still travelling, with the hold-up horses too far back to close the gap. His style-fit discount is real but the race shape is so tailored to his position that the probability cannot be ignored.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough and the ground dries to quick enough that hold-up horses travelling into it can finish past tiring prominent types.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability shape given how many of the supposed closers are redistributed horses who are unlikely to be sitting deep enough to produce a true late run. Nothing Hectic, Moonshine Girl and Cornaroya Rocco are the truest hold-up types who might benefit if they do find themselves in the right position late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field creates scrimmaging, pace injected by secondary movers and a more end-to-end gallop than anticipated.
scenarios.body: In a race this size, traffic problems and a busier early pace can compress the field and bring more diverse profiles into contention, allowing a handicapper catching a good mark to emerge. Pilgrims Walk and Tannery Park, both on long layoffs, could outrun their prices if freshness proves an asset over this stamina trip.

watchPoints.text: Joshua Chamberlain's unchallenged lead is the race-defining factor — if he is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop unchecked, prominent trackers It's Time Again and Ranger Billy are perfectly placed to pounce, so watch whether anything attempts to go with him in the first mile.

The large field of 19 over 2m6½f at Ballinrobe creates a significant traffic risk for the redistributed hold-up horses — watch Moonshine Girl and Nothing Hectic specifically; if they get trapped wide or blocked turning for home, their chance evaporates regardless of finishing speed.

Tannery Park returns from 440 days off and must be watched in the early stages for signs of ring-rustiness — a horse who fades in the finish after a long layoff over a stamina trip is a potential faller risk or may pull up if the race comes too soon.

Everystep Oftheway has not raced in 763 days and has no jockey confirmed — watch for any late market moves that suggest connections have strong confidence, otherwise treat as a complete unknown that could affect running room for others early.

With so many hold-up horses fighting for the same rear-field ground, watch the pace through the first half of the race — if It's Time Again or Ranger Billy push forward more aggressively than expected, this could inject a secondary pace injection that fundamentally changes the shape and brings genuine closers into play.
